title: Great App, But Still Stuck in the Cloud
text:
This is a follow-up to my first review, “Great App, But Still Stuck in the Cloud.” Well, guess what—I finally clicked the “iCloud Drive” button in the app… and surprise! It wasn’t some exclusive cloud vault or premium add-on. It was just the iPad’s regular Files app, hiding behind a fancy name and a cloud emoji like it’s in costume for Halloween.

I’ve been copying and pasting scripts like it’s 2005, avoiding that button because it screamed “login required” or “subscribe now.” Turns out it was the one place I actually needed to go.

So yeah, now that I know the trick, the app works like a charm. Voice tracking is great, scrolling is smooth, and once your script’s in there, you’re golden.

But c’mon devs—next time just label it “Files / iCloud” or something clear. Don’t make me play ding-dong ditch with my own documents.

Bumped it up to 4 stars because the app is good—but I had to unlock it like it was a side quest in a video game.



Origin review…Look, PromptSmart Pro has been around longer than most influencers’ careers, and the voice-tracking teleprompter feature? Chef’s kiss. It works like a charm, even when I mumble like I’m auditioning for a mumblecore film.

But here’s the part that makes me tilt my head like a confused dog: Why, in the year 2026, can I still not just open a file from my iPad’s local storage? Why must I go on a scavenger hunt through cloud syncing, account logins, and monthly upsell traps just to load a simple script?

It’s like buying a microwave that only works if you subscribe to a cloud-based kitchen. I paid $29 one-time for this thing, and now you want me to pay more just to sync or upload a file? The app already lives on my device. My files are right there. Just let me open one. Revolutionary, I know.

Bottom line: It mostly works as promised, but it’s wrapped in a monetization scheme that feels more 2012 startup than 2026 usability. Lose the cloud dependency for basic features, and you’ll have a perfect 5-star tool. Until then, I’ll keep yelling at my iPad while activating my “extended intro trial” for the 9th time.
I should get an add on just for this review alone!  

Tommy Gunn

text:

As a couple examples:

-Perhaps even more frustrating is that the text very often stops scrolling when using voice tracking.
-When creating a script, it asks for a story title, but does not auto select the box or bring up your keyboard. If you click the script box, it will skip naming your script.

As far as QoL, settings should save between videos. Every time I open a new script to film, I have to find a text color that shows up over my camera footage. Alternatively, I’d love to see a separate setting for text background color. I can often see myself squinting to read in my footage.

Finally, it was not apparent anywhere that this app would not support external mics. It turns out, iPhone often has capability issues between apps and external mics. Guess I should chalk that up to an iOS issue.

However, quite frustrating that I had to discover this for myself. I had reached out to customer service who made me feel like I was to blame for the technical difficulties. Then, they ghosted me before I went off to discover this problem on my own.

Guess I’d just like to see more transparency since this is in fact an app to help with recording.

title: Could be great, but REALLY needs work!
text:
The voice tracking functionality in this app is very clever, and it works well “most” of the time. But even after following all their formatting recommendations, there are still times when the script will suddenly scroll way off the current section you’re on, forcing you to manually scroll back to find where it’s supposed to be. This can create massive panic during a live presentation! 

Updates to PromptSmart are on a much, much slower cycle than my other apps. There are tons of things that could be tweaked and improved, which makes me wonder why the developer isn’t more aggressive in releasing regular updates and enhancements. If he’s short on things to do, here’s a list to get him going: 
The macOS PromptSmart editor app is… well… it’s awful to use. It doesn’t look, feel or function like a native Mac app at all. I get the impression that it was just ported over from Windows and made to operate on the Mac. No true Mac enthusiast would ever feel at home using this poorly cobbled-together piece of junk. 
In fact, that app is so awful that I’d rather use their web-based editor… which also has a slew of frustrations. The biggest problem is that the actual editor window is, for some insane reason, squashed into a very narrow column all the way over on the right-hand side of the browser. Two thirds of the browser width is unused, forcing you to edit your scripts in a tiny, cramped column way over on the right side. What the heck, guys?! Surely you can come up with a better solution than this!
PromptSmart on the iPad has no Dark Mode when viewing scripts. It’s incredibly distracting to go from a nice black background when actually running a script, to suddenly being blinded by a glaring white screen after exiting that script and returning to the sync window. Seriously, it’s 2021… Dark Mode should be in every app by now. 
There’s a massive bug I found right before walking on stage for a live presentation, and it almost destroyed my ability to read the script. I discovered that if you edit a synced script on the iPad and then save it, PromptSmart inserts random blank lines throughout your entire script! What a flippin’ nightmare! So now, I only edit scripts in the web browser on my Mac because I never want that to happen again, but that means I can never make last-minute edits on my iPad. I’ve tested this with multiple scripts and it is a definite bug that needs to be fixed ASAP!
The sync dates shown on the iPad are in dd/mm/yyyy format, even though that’s not the format used in the USA. Why can’t PromptSmart automatically determine the local date format setting on my devices as being mm/dd/yyyy like all my other apps do?
Without telling you or asking for permission, PromptSmart creates a folder in your Mac’s root folder called psmart-workspace. Again, my other apps don’t do this because this is not standard macOS protocol. Clearly the developer is not a Mac guy. 
All in all this is a good app, but for the annual fee, it really needs to be cleaned up a lot more. And here’s a friendly word of warning to all users — you’d better always keep a backup copy of your script with you on paper before you go on stage, because there is every chance PromptSmart will glitch, go off track or mess up your script, leaving you scrambling in front of the crowd.

title: Great... but extremely unreliable
text:
I’m a full time content creator on YouTube and decided to finally invest in a teleprompter to reduce overall production time and make batch shooting easier. The other app (BestView) that was recommended for use with the teleprompter was ok but lacked some of the more advanced features I was looking for like being able to narrow the side margins to minimize eye drifting. I had heard of Promptsmart Pro and decided to give it a shot as I was intrigued by the voice recognition and figured that if that didn’t work well for my needs, I could simply use it in scrolling mode and wouldn’t feel as though I wasted $20. Boy, was I wrong.

As I said, I was intrigued by the voice recognition aspect of the app and knew that, as with any voice recognition, there will be some issues here and there (Siri not being able to decipher simple words). I’m ok with that, it being a finicky technology in the first place. But I felt that since I have fairly decent dictation and enunciation and I tend to project my voice more when on camera, that maybe it would works pretty well for me. 

My initial read through went fine with no issues other than a common one: skipping ahead. Ok, no problem, formatting can cause issues so I’ll use the clear formatting tool in Google Docs as that’s where I write my scripts anyway. I also took out spaces between paragraphs, thinking that could be an issue as well. No dice. The skipping persisted. I also tried abbreviations for words I used commonly, and since I do tech videos, there are a lot of terms may use in a video when I’m trying to hammer something home. Again, that didn’t help either, and actually made things worse.

Okay. So I gave the voice recognition a shot and it didn’t work that well. No big deal. I figured as such. I’ll just use the pre-set scroll speed and find the speed that fits my voice. It was all great until.... it started skipping ahead. On the pre-set scroll speed. Okay, maybe it was a fluke. Nope. It happened again, this time in a different spot. 

I noticed the app was still using the microphone (the green dot in the upper right) so I figured maybe it was getting confused somehow by trying to recognize my voice. So I disabled it in the app settings on my iPhone. This actually won’t work at all, as even with a pre-set scroll speed, the app REQUIRES access to your microphone. What!? I don’t want or need to use the mic for the preset scroll speed. So my troubleshooting steps went nowhere with that. As a last resort, I uninstalled and reinstalled and had the issue remains. 

So yeah, overall, I paid $20 for an app that was supposed to reduce my production time but instead has LENGTHENED it by ruining takes that were otherwise fine. As of right now, this app is unusable in its current state and I’ve gone back to using the app that was recommend by the teleprompter manufacturer. I do see that their support is active on here, so if they reach out and help to minimize this issue or at least make the pre-set scrolling not skip ahead,  I’ll happily edit this review and change my rating. I’m not even interested in a refund, I just really would love this app to work properly.

title: Great app, until it isn’t...
text:
I have used this app for years. I have a recording studio in my backyard where I record video and audio in an isolated environment with high end audio equipment. The promise of the VoiceTrack feature is really the headline feature on this app. But today is the last straw for me. 

I have spent so many hours in frustration with this app. It widens the line between failure and amazement. When it works, I love it—as other reviewers have said. When it doesn’t work, which is often, I want to throw my phone out the window. 

I don’t want to email support. I don’t want to tweet at them. I want the app to deliver on its promise. I paid for it, and it almost lives up to its marketing. But that “almost” is so painful. 

I thought I could solve the voice tracking problem with the remote app, but that’s another $2/month. Sounds cheap, but I don’t want to give this company money to fix a feature that disappoints me to no end.

I have had people in my studio to film them using this app and I end up having to use my finger to move the script along. What’s the point?

It is rare that I write an app review. But here I am. Frustrated to no end at myself for believing this app was better than it is. In the end, I’m the idiot.

title: Unpredictable Behavior
text:
The idea of this is great, but the execution is inconsistent. After trying out the free version, and being impressed with its ability to flow with your speech, I went ahead and paid for it. Unfortunately, as I got to using it more, it has proven to work inconsistently. 

The main issue is that the app doesn’t actually always follow your speaking. It will go along for awhile working flawlessly, then it will just stop and not scroll anymore. Sometimes I can get it scrolling again by going back and re-reading the last paragraph. Other times, I have to stop it completely and start again. 

The most common problem is having it stop while I’m reading, but it also sometimes will be moving along perfectly, and then just skip ahead a couple of pages. Both of these are really frustrating.

Yes, I can stop and restart from the previous paragraph, but I hate that about 75% of the times I have to stop and restart, it is because the teleprompter messed up. The other 25% are my own mistakes, but it would be nice if I only had to reshoot 25% of what I do now.

I took note that the sound can make it unreliable, but I plug a shotgun mic into my iPad Pro to be sure it can hear.

It’s really impressive that it can do this auto scrolling thing at all, so I am impressed. However, it just messes up,
 too much. I hope it improves, because I really need it.
